title: Persist profile-based contract authorization and PR review state
description:
Durable, repo-wide contract-authorization and PR-review system, created because
PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED with no mechanism able to state,
authorize, or invalidate a change-specific review contract. Foundation 1
(eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14) R3 records the blocking consequence: F1 must CONSUME an
external eshyra-review-checkpoint binding
{reviewedHeadSha, contractHash, procedureIds[], reviewerRole, result,
implementationPermission} and is forbidden from building it. This bead builds
it, once, for the whole repository.

ONE lifecycle repo-wide; evidence requirements selected by REVIEW PROFILE.
Ordinary Eshyra work is NOT rules-pack work: standard < semantic-system <
rules-clause-complete. Foundation 1 is rules-clause-complete. This bead is
semantic-system.

Beads are the authoritative location for change-specific review contracts. PR
bodies and templates are explanatory only. No per-bead committed contract file.

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-review-v2

### Review classification
- Declared profile: semantic-system
- Authorization required before implementation: yes
- Classification reason: This change creates the repository's evidence and
  review-governance system: persisted PR review state, authority boundaries,
  deterministic identity and hashing, and fail-closed CI gating. It is durable
  trust-boundary infrastructure, not rules-source work. It touches no rules
  source, no importer, and no generated pack record, so rules-clause-complete
  does not apply. Revision 2 additionally revises the minimum-profile policy to
  cover executable agent-authority surfaces, and revises the contract-hash
  function; both are material and both are declared below.
- Change characteristics: authorization-or-evidence-boundary-change;
  public-schema-or-protocol-change
- Escalation conditions: Escalate to rules-clause-complete if any change under
  packages/core/scripts/importers, packages/core/src/rules, or
  packages/core/data/rules-packs enters scope, or if the work begins asserting
  source-obligation, pack-membership, or engine-capability semantics rather
  than transporting reviewer-published evidence about them.
- Owning Bead: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.17
- Contract revision: 2. Supersedes revision 1
  (ff5e2eb3bd75448b6faa0cc77443709c539f537869e4264b9ec556125c0f8309), which was
  reviewed at head 1579b9835347422ef23d6045027143728ec44ea3 with result
  changes-requested and materialContractChange true. Revision 2 incorporates ten
  established defect classes D1-D10 and is a MATERIAL change: it moves the
  contract hash, mandates a policy change that moves the policy hash, and
  changes the contract-hash function itself. All prior authorization state is
  void. Fresh full contract authorization is required before implementation
  resumes.
- Bootstrap transition: This remains the one-time process bootstrap PR. The
  bootstrap exception is bounded, waives ONLY the otherwise-impossible
  pre-existing authorization checkpoint, authorizes nothing, and approves
  nothing. Revision 2 narrows it further under D4 and D5: it must fail closed on
  any unresolved predicate, and it may never produce a lifecycle state, output
  string, or CI conclusion containing "authorized".

### Objective and scope
- Intended outcome: One durable, versioned, machine-enforced review lifecycle
  that (a) selects a review profile from changed paths plus declared change
  characteristics, (b) validates exactly one normative bead REVIEW CONTRACT,
  (c) publishes contract handoffs and reviewer checkpoints as PR comments,
  (d) distinguishes contract authorization from implementation review, (e)
  detects staleness by hash and head SHA, (f) makes DESIGN_INVALIDATED a
  terminal state, and (g) states truthfully, at every surface, exactly which of
  its claims are machine-enforced and which rest on manual owner attestation.
- In scope: docs/review protocol and three profile documents; the
  machine-readable minimum-profile policy; reusable TypeScript modules under
  packages/core/scripts/review; npm scripts review:classify, review:preflight,
  review:handoff, review:checkpoint, review:invalidate, review:ci; PR CI
  enforcing the lifecycle; a trusted-context refresh path for comment changes;
  concise pointers in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; unit tests behind injectable
  GitHub and Beads boundaries; test-fixture isolation; and the ten defect-class
  remediations D1-D10 below.
- Out of scope: Foundation 1 implementation of any kind; any change to
  generated SRD pack output; reopening, modifying, or republishing state for
  PRs #475, #476, or #477; a general workflow engine; branch-protection
  automation; hosted review tooling; migration of historical PRs; and any
  cryptographic, signed, or GitHub-App-backed reviewer-identity mechanism,
  which is future protocol work under a later protocol version.
- Exact affected surfaces: docs/review/**; packages/core/scripts/review/**;
  packages/core/test/review/**; packages/core/test/fixtures/review/**;
  package.json scripts; .github/workflows/review-governance.yml; AGENTS.md;
  CLAUDE.md.

### Authority and inputs
- Authoritative inputs: The owning bead's single normative "## REVIEW CONTRACT"
  block, retrieved from the Beads database, is the authority for
  change-specific requirements. docs/review/minimum-profile-policy.json is the
  authority for the minimum profile. The protocol and profile documents under
  docs/review are the authority for the lifecycle and the evidence bar. The
  independent reviewer's verdict, transported as a checkpoint comment and
  attested by the repository owner, is the authority for authorization and
  approval. The PR head SHA and changed-path set reported by GitHub are the
  authority for what is being reviewed.
- Derived inputs: protocol hash, selected-profile hash, policy hash, normalized
  contract hash, review-artifact digest, path-derived minimum profile,
  characteristic-derived minimum profile, effective profile, and every
  lifecycle state label. All are computed, never stored in the contract, and
  never author-asserted.
- Untrusted inputs: PR title, PR body, PR template checkboxes, branch names,
  commit messages, comment prose outside the canonical marker envelope, bead
  notes not named by the contract, bead TITLE, escalation reason text, any
  display string interpolated into a published comment, environment variables,
  and CI job success. None may grant authorization, satisfy an evidence
  requirement, or influence machine payload parsing.
- Ownership: This bead owns the protocol, the profile documents, the policy, the
  parser and normalizer, the checkpoint schemas, the comment markers and the
  machine envelope, the commands, the CI gate, and the trusted refresh path. It
  does not own any profile's domain evidence standards beyond stating them;
  rules-source semantics remain owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14 and its successors.

### Behavior and representation
- Required behavior: Parse exactly one normative contract per bead. Normalize it
  deterministically into a canonical structure and hash it with SHA-256 over an
  RFC 8785 JCS serialization of NFC-normalized text. Reject duplicate semantic
  keys rather than committing to them. Compute the effective profile as the
  stricter of the declared profile and the minimum profile derived from paths
  and declared characteristics. Publish exactly one active
  eshyra-review-contract:v2 comment per PR, idempotently upserted, carrying its
  machine payload in an unambiguous marker-bound envelope. Parse checkpoint
  comments into typed contract-authorization or implementation-review
  checkpoints under an explicit authority mode. Treat any design-invalidation
  marker as terminal at every command and every output mode. Re-evaluate
  governance whenever authoritative comment state changes.
- Required distinctions: contract authorization versus implementation review;
  declared versus minimum versus effective profile; publication head versus
  reviewed head; material contract change versus ordinary implementation churn;
  path-derived versus characteristic-derived escalation; production versus
  fixture-only checkpoints; a hash constant matching versus a review having
  occurred; MACHINE-ENFORCED structural validity versus MANUALLY ATTESTED
  reviewer authority; what local preflight proves versus what CI proves versus
  what only the independent reviewer can establish; a resolved empty result
  versus an unresolved lookup; and a bootstrap waiver versus an authorization.
- Compatibility requirements: The protocol identifier eshyra-review-v2 and the
  profile identifiers standard-v1, semantic-system-v1, and
  rules-clause-complete-v1 remain stable across this revision. The normalization
  change in D8 and the policy change in D9 deliberately move published hashes
  and therefore void outstanding authorizations; that is the intended
  behavior, not a regression. Any future change to normalization rules,
  required-field sets, checkpoint schemas, the machine envelope, or the policy
  likewise voids outstanding authorizations and requires a versioned changelog
  entry in the protocol document.
- Negative behavior: Under-classification is rejected. A missing, duplicated,
  placeholder-only, or profile-inconsistent contract is rejected. A contract
  containing duplicate semantic keys is rejected rather than hashed. A
  checkpoint whose hashes or effective profile disagree with current state is
  stale and rejected. A partial-scope authorization grants nothing. A
  self-contradictory checkpoint is rejected. An unresolved lookup is an error,
  never an empty set and never a default classification. A comment carrying more
  than one candidate machine payload, or a malformed envelope, is rejected. No
  environment variable, flag, or path enables fixture acceptance in production.
  No output at any surface claims that reviewer identity or independence was
  machine-verified.

### Consumers and blast radius
- Direct consumers: every future PR in this repository; the review-governance CI
  workflow and its trusted refresh path; agents following AGENTS.md and
  CLAUDE.md; Foundation 1 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14), which consumes
  contract-authorization checkpoints and fails closed without one.
- Indirect consumers: all beads blocked on Foundation 1; the F1-A/F1-B
  decomposition to be created after this PR merges; every later foundation that
  needs an independent approval record rather than a self-asserted one; and any
  future signed or GitHub-App-backed authority mode, which must be able to
  replace manual-owner-attestation without redefining the lifecycle.
- Cross-surface checks: npm scripts resolve; the CI workflow calls only the
  published commands; the protocol and profile documents are the exact files
  hashed by the code; the policy file parses under the schema the tests assert;
  root instruction files stay within the size ceiling; and every lifecycle
  predicate renders identically across the lifecycle enum, human output, JSON
  output, CI conclusion, handoff display, checkpoint display, and next-action
  text.
- Migration implications: There is no prior review state to migrate, and none is
  preserved: revision 2 voids every hash published under revision 1. The
  handoff published at head 1579b98 becomes stale by construction and must be
  republished after re-authorization. PRs #475/#476/#477 remain terminal and are
  used only as regression fixtures. The gate applies to PRs opened or updated
  after merge.

### Failure, recovery, and residuals
- Fail-closed requirements: Every command exits nonzero on a malformed, stale,
  duplicated, under-classified, or contradictory contract or checkpoint, and on
  a design-invalidated PR. Every evaluation path that cannot resolve its
  authoritative input returns a typed unresolved error and never an
  empty-but-successful result; this covers changed-path discovery, base-ref and
  protocol-path lookup, bead retrieval, GitHub retrieval, and comment
  enumeration. A bootstrap predicate that cannot be resolved defeats the waiver.
  Production checkpoint loading rejects fixture-marked content unconditionally.
  Ambiguous machine-payload framing is rejected rather than resolved by
  position.
- Recovery or rollback: Recovery from a rejected state is republication, never
  suppression: correct the bead contract, re-run review:classify and
  review:preflight, republish the handoff, and obtain a fresh checkpoint. A
  material contract change requires re-authorization before substantive
  implementation resumes. There is no recovery from DESIGN_INVALIDATED for that
  PR; recovery is a successor bead and a new PR.
- Approved residuals: Reviewer identity and independence are NOT machine-
  verified under authority mode manual-owner-attestation; this is an accepted,
  explicitly disclosed limitation, not a defect, and the tooling must say so
  rather than imply otherwise. CI cannot prove that a published handoff was
  derived from the live bead; it validates a self-published copy and must say
  exactly that. Branch-protection rules cannot be configured from this
  repository and remain a manual owner step; the gate is advisory until a
  repository administrator makes the check required. Historical PRs are not
  retrofitted.
- Explicitly unsupported material: multi-repository review state; cryptographic
  signing of checkpoints; an authenticated reviewer principal distinct from the
  repository owner; automatic closing or mutation of PRs and beads; fork-PR
  privileged execution; and approval of a PR by any automated actor. Reviewer
  identity verification is no longer listed as merely unsupported: it is
  replaced by an explicit, declared manual trust model whose limits every
  surface must state.

### Verification and closure
- Required tests: every test required by revision 1 (contract extraction,
  per-profile required sections, missing and duplicate contracts,
  placeholder-only fields, deterministic normalization and hashing, profile
  ordering, path-derived and characteristic-derived escalation, voluntary
  over-classification, under-classification rejection, changed-profile and
  changed-policy invalidation, handoff formatting and idempotent upsert,
  authorization freshness, optional standard authorization, mandatory
  semantic-system and rules-clause authorization, implementation head freshness,
  incomplete-scope rejection, checkpoint-kind separation, new-defect-class
  transition, terminal design-invalidation, attempted approval after
  invalidation, fixture isolation, bootstrap-exception isolation, stale
  protocol/profile/policy detection, unrelated-path standard classification,
  malformed-comment parsing, duplicate and superseded comment handling, compact
  default output, verbose and JSON output, effective-profile-only reading
  guidance, and root instruction size ceilings), PLUS the permanent regression
  obligations R1-R10 stated under each defect class below.
- Permanent regression evidence: all of the above live under
  packages/core/test/review and run in the default vitest suite. They are
  permanent, not one-off. PRs #475/#476/#477 supply the design-invalidated
  regression fixture. Each defect class D1-D10 must fail its regression test
  when its fix is reverted.
- Generated or exact membership: not applicable - this change asserts no
  source-obligation, pack-record, or engine-capability membership. It transports
  and validates reviewer-published evidence about such claims.
- Closure evidence: npm run verify:worktree green from the owning worktree;
  bd dep cycles clean; an open, unmerged PR carrying a fresh full
  semantic-system implementation review at the then-current head under contract
  revision 2 or later; and the final report items enumerated in the protocol
  document.

### Semantic-system contract
- Trust boundaries: AUTHORITY MODE IS manual-owner-attestation. (1) CI
  machine-enforces exactly: contract and checkpoint schema validity;
  deterministic hashes; profile calculation; head and contract freshness; legal
  lifecycle transitions; fixture rejection; terminal invalidation; and
  internally consistent handoff and checkpoint state. (2) Local review:preflight
  additionally compares the LIVE bead contract against the published handoff,
  and only where Beads access exists. (3) CI CANNOT independently prove that a
  handoff was derived from the live bead, and no component may state or imply
  that it did. (4) The independent reviewer MUST read the authoritative bead
  contract and bind its contract hash and reviewed scope in the verdict. (5) The
  repository owner is the manual trust root, publishing or causing publication
  of an exact reviewer-produced checkpoint. (6) The tooling must NEVER claim
  reviewer identity or independence was machine-verified. (7) reviewerRole, the
  GitHub comment author, and publisherLogin are DESCRIPTIVE EVIDENCE ONLY. (8) A
  structurally valid checkpoint under this mode means "review record accepted
  under manual owner attestation", never "independent reviewer identity
  verified". The producer of an artifact still may not define the standard its
  own output is judged by; under this mode that separation is upheld by the
  owner's attestation and the reviewer's reading of the bead, not by machine
  identity checks - and that is exactly what must be disclosed.
- Stable identities and revisions: protocol identifier eshyra-review-v2; profile
  identifiers standard-v1, semantic-system-v1, rules-clause-complete-v1; the
  three canonical comment markers. Four SHA-256 digests carry semantic revision:
  protocol, selected profile, policy, normalized contract - all over NFC-
  normalized input per D8. A fifth digest, reviewArtifactDigest, binds the exact
  transported review result; it proves transport integrity ONLY and does NOT
  prove authorship, which must be stated wherever it is surfaced. Full 64-hex
  digests are authoritative; truncation is display-only. Checkpoints additionally
  carry authorityMode, identityAssurance, and publisherLogin per D3.
- State transitions and lifecycle: design-invalidated (terminal, absorbing, and
  enforced by EVERY command in EVERY output mode); authorization-pending;
  authorized-and-in-progress; ready-for-implementation-review;
  changes-requested; implementation-approved. Bootstrap adds a disjoint family
  that must never contain the substring "authorized" in any surfaced form:
  bootstrap-authorization-waived; ready-for-bootstrap-implementation-review;
  implementation-approved-under-bootstrap-review. Legal transitions are
  enumerated in code, not prose. Any new commit invalidates implementation
  approval; later implementation commits do NOT invalidate contract
  authorization while contract, profile, and policy hashes are unchanged. Every
  authoritative comment change forces re-evaluation per D1. Handoff replacement
  is an in-place upsert of exactly one active comment; superseded or malformed
  handoff comments are reported as defects, never silently ignored, and
  publication must not overwrite a malformed comment that may be evidence.
- Stale-state detection: a checkpoint is stale when any published hash, or the
  effective profile, disagrees with current computed state; an implementation
  checkpoint is additionally stale when its reviewed head is not the current
  head; a handoff is stale when its published hashes or, for implementation
  handoffs, its head no longer match. A previously computed CI conclusion is
  itself stale state: it must be recomputed on authoritative comment change, and
  a stale-green or stale-red check is a defect (D1).
- Migration and backward compatibility: revision 2 voids all revision-1 hashes
  by design. A future protocol revision must bump the protocol identifier and
  marker version and add a changelog entry; silent migration of contracts or
  checkpoints is prohibited. Reading a marker or envelope version this
  implementation does not understand is an error, never a skip. A future
  authority mode stronger than manual-owner-attestation must be additive: it
  changes authorityMode and identityAssurance without redefining the lifecycle.
- Adversarial scenarios: a PR author publishing their own approval checkpoint; a
  hostile bead title, escalation reason, or display string containing Markdown
  fences or JSON attempting to shadow a machine payload (D10); an author editing
  the contract after authorization; an author lowering the declared profile; an
  author editing or deleting a checkpoint comment after a green check (D1); a
  fixture checkpoint copied into a real PR; an environment variable used to relax
  the gate; the bootstrap exception invoked for a second bead, a second PR,
  another repository, or a fork head (D5); an unfetched or ambiguous base ref
  activating the bootstrap waiver (D5); a git failure silently producing an empty
  changed-path set and a standard classification (D6); a duplicate semantic key
  making one value drive classification while another is displayed as
  authoritative (D7); NFC/NFD-equivalent text moving a contract hash (D8); an
  agent-authority change under .claude/** classified as standard (D9); a second
  active handoff shadowing the first; a superseded checkpoint read as current; a
  malformed comment silently treated as absent; and a fork PR attempting
  privileged execution.

### Established defect classes
- D1 authoritative-comment refresh: INVARIANT - every change to authoritative
  handoff, checkpoint, or invalidation state must refresh the derived governance
  result; a prior conclusion must never survive a later terminal or
  approval-state change. SURFACES - the CI workflow, review:ci, and every
  handoff, checkpoint, and invalidation publication or editing path. BEHAVIOR -
  governance must re-evaluate on comment created, edited, and deleted, covering
  at least red-then-approved, green-then-DESIGN_INVALIDATED, a corrected handoff
  with no code commit, an edited or superseded checkpoint, and both stale-green
  and stale-red checks. The refresh must run in a TRUSTED EXECUTION PATH that
  never runs untrusted PR code with privileged credentials: the comment-driven
  job must execute only base-branch-trusted code, must not check out or execute
  PR head content, and must publish its result as a status against the head SHA;
  pull_request_target with a PR-head checkout is prohibited. Refresh failure
  must surface as failure, with defined retry semantics, never as a passing or
  absent check. R1 - an event matrix proving create, edit, and delete of each
  authoritative comment kind recomputes state, including stale-green and
  stale-red cases, and proving the refresh path executes no PR-head code.
- D2 bead-to-handoff authority boundary: INVARIANT - no component may claim CI
  verified the handoff against the live bead. SURFACES - review:preflight,
  review:handoff, review:ci, ciGate, workflow status text, merge-readiness
  interpretation, all JSON output. BEHAVIOR - each surface must state exactly
  what it proves: preflight proves handoff-equals-bead where Beads access
  exists; CI proves published state is structurally consistent, current, and
  sufficient for the stage; the reviewer must read the bead and bind its
  contract hash and reviewed scope. Unresolved bead or GitHub state fails closed
  and never becomes empty membership or a valid default. A bead contract edited
  without republishing the handoff must be detectable by preflight and must not
  read as current. R2 - tests asserting the exact claim strings at every surface,
  that no surface asserts live-bead verification, and that unresolved bead or
  GitHub access produces a typed failure.
- D3 reviewer and publisher authority: INVARIANT - a structurally valid
  checkpoint means "review record accepted under manual owner attestation", never
  "independent reviewer identity verified". SURFACES - review:checkpoint, the
  checkpoint parser, publication, discovery, computePrReviewState,
  mergeReadiness, CI output, JSON output. BEHAVIOR - checkpoints carry
  authorityMode (manual-owner-attestation), identityAssurance
  (not-machine-verified), reviewArtifactDigest, and publisherLogin.
  reviewArtifactDigest binds the exact transported review result and does not
  prove its authorship; that limitation is surfaced wherever the digest is.
  reviewerRole, comment author, and publisherLogin are descriptive evidence only
  and are recorded, surfaced, and never used as a gate. Approval under this mode
  means: the owner attests that the bound review artifact is the independent
  reviewer's verdict over the bound contract hash and scope. R3 - tests proving a
  role/author mismatch cannot become machine-verified approval, that every
  approval surface is labelled with its authority mode and identity assurance,
  and that no output asserts verified independence.
- D4 bootstrap state consistency: INVARIANT - authorizationSatisfied === false
  implies no surfaced state may contain "authorized". SURFACES - state, report,
  preflight JSON, CI JSON and conclusion, handoff display, checkpoint display,
  next-action text. BEHAVIOR - the bootstrap family
  (bootstrap-authorization-waived, ready-for-bootstrap-implementation-review,
  implementation-approved-under-bootstrap-review) is disjoint from the
  authorized family; the checkpoint formatter names an implementation verdict
  "verdict", never unconditionally "approval"; and handoff-published
  declaredProfile, minimumProfile, profileId, effectiveProfile, and
  authorizationRequired are cross-checked against the embedded contract and the
  computed classification rather than accepted as assertions. R4 - a cross-
  surface truth table asserting identical predicates across every surface, and
  asserting the invariant above.
- D5 bootstrap containment and base-state failures: INVARIANT - the exception
  requires all intended predicates simultaneously and fails closed when any is
  unresolved. SURFACES - bootstrap, the base-path lookup, local preflight, the CI
  gate, fork-PR behavior. BEHAVIOR - predicates extend to repository identity,
  PR identity or an immutable bootstrap identity, same-repository head, expected
  base branch, non-fork head, and the exact bead and branch. A protocol-path
  lookup error, a missing or unfetched base ref, unavailable PR metadata, or any
  unresolved predicate defeats the waiver; a lookup error must never read as
  "protocol absent". R5 - an eligibility matrix over repository, PR, same-repo
  head, expected base, exact bead, exact branch, protocol-presence resolution,
  malformed state, fork state, second-PR attempts, and lookup errors.
- D6 fail-closed changed-path calculation: INVARIANT - an evaluation path that
  cannot resolve its authoritative input must fail, not return an empty
  successful result. SURFACES - review:classify and review:preflight without
  --pr, pre-implementation authorization decisions, the agent entry workflow, and
  every other unresolved lookup returning a valid-looking empty value. BEHAVIOR -
  changed-path discovery returns a typed resolved(paths) or unresolved(error);
  merge-base, diff, and status failures are errors with nonzero exit; no
  unresolved state may produce a standard classification. The GitHub changed-file
  boundary must state and test its pagination guarantee for large PRs. R6 - tests
  proving each git failure mode exits nonzero and that no unresolved state
  yields standard, plus a large-PR pagination test.
- D7 duplicate semantic fields: INVARIANT - a normalized contract has exactly one
  unambiguous value per normative key. SURFACES - normalizeContractBlock,
  validateContractStructure, contract hashing, handoff publication, CI contract
  reconstruction, authorization freshness. BEHAVIOR - duplicate preamble keys,
  duplicate section titles, and duplicate field keys are REJECTED, not preserved;
  no value may be selected by field order; and no contract containing duplicates
  may be hashed or rendered into an authoritative handoff. Coverage includes
  duplicate declared profile, authorization requirement, owning bead, protocol,
  change characteristics, and every profile-specific required field. R7 - exact
  rejection tests for each duplicate identity kind and for a duplicate whose
  first and later values disagree.
- D8 Unicode normalization: INVARIANT - canonically equivalent text has one
  identity. SURFACES - contract normalization and hashing, document hashing, the
  protocol document, and the tests. BEHAVIOR - NFC is applied to contract text
  before canonicalization and hashing, matching document hashing; the protocol
  document states which strings are normalized; identifier-valued fields
  (protocol, declared profile, owning bead, change characteristics) additionally
  validate against a restricted character set rather than relying on
  normalization alone. Protocol, implementation, and tests must agree. This moves
  existing hashes and is explicitly material. R8 - NFC/NFD equivalence tests for
  contract hashing alongside the existing wrapping, whitespace, list-marker, and
  delimiter-bearing-value stability tests.
- D9 minimum-profile policy coverage: INVARIANT - the repository-calculated
  minimum independently catches representative semantic and trust-boundary
  changes without relying on a voluntary characteristic declaration. SURFACES -
  minimum-profile-policy.json, the policy tests, and the live agent-authority
  paths. BEHAVIOR - add a semantic-system rule covering executable agent
  authority and policy injection, justified per path rather than blanket-
  escalated: .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks/** (hook registration and
  the fail-closed supervisor gate that grants dispatch, branch, and push
  authority); AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (the repository's normative agent
  instructions, including the standing push and PR authority); and
  .github/workflows/** (CI execution and token permissions). None of these is
  rules-clause-complete, because none asserts source, pack, or engine semantics.
  .github/pull_request_template.md and .github/dependabot.yml remain standard,
  the template because the protocol makes it explanatory only. Changing the
  policy moves the policy hash and invalidates prior authorization. R9 -
  historical-fixture tests binding changed-path memberships to expected profiles
  for representative merged PRs, including PR #468 as semantic-system, ordinary
  documentation as standard, provider-neutral orchestrator work as
  semantic-system, and pack-driven runtime work as rules-clause-complete.
- D10 unambiguous machine-payload framing: INVARIANT - a comment has exactly one
  machine payload, located by an unforgeable marker-bound envelope and never by
  the position of a generic Markdown fence. SURFACES - the marker module,
  handoff and checkpoint and invalidation formatters and parsers, and every
  interpolated display string. BEHAVIOR - the payload is delimited by an
  envelope bound to the canonical marker, of the form
  "<!-- eshyra-review-payload:v1:begin -->" then a fenced json block then
  "<!-- eshyra-review-payload:v1:end -->", parsed by locating the envelope
  delimiters and never by scanning for the first fence. Exactly one envelope may
  appear per comment; zero, two or more, unterminated, nested, or malformed
  envelopes fail closed. Every interpolated display string - bead title,
  escalation reason, bead id, reviewer role, scope notes, invalidation reason -
  is neutralized before rendering such that it cannot introduce an envelope
  delimiter, and the formatter and parser round-trip arbitrary hostile display
  text. An attacker-controlled title containing Markdown fences or JSON must not
  change the parsed handoff kind, head, hashes, contract, or profile. R10 -
  round-trip tests over hostile display strings including fenced JSON and forged
  envelope delimiters; multiple-candidate-payload and malformed-envelope
  fail-closed tests; and a regression reproducing the observed shadowing, in
  which a bead title carrying a fenced payload flipped a published
  contract-authorization handoff at one head into an implementation-review
  handoff at another while still validating.
